newsitem.title: UK: ScotAm again rejects Abbey National bid.
newsitem.headline: ScotAm again rejects Abbey National bid.

text.p: Scottish Amicable, the mutually-owned life assurance group, again rejected Abbey National's takeover approach on Friday descibing it as "unsolicited" and "of uncertain value".

The group said the circular to shareholders outlining its own proposals to drop its mutual status and float on the stock market due to be released in two weeks time would confirm the embedded value of the company at a "conservative' one billion stg.
"Abbey National's unsolicited proposal is of uncertain value and has been rejected," said a spokesman for the group's advisers.
"There is a grave danger of policyholders being misled by the vague terms of Abbey National's pronouncements. They have misunderstood Scottish Amicable's proposals."
The spokesman said the 200 million pound benefits payable on flotation quoted by Abbey National was the minimum value predicted.
The actual value, he said, would be considerably higher.
